title: Onramp Ecosystem Pulse Check — SDKs, Quickstarts, and Samples
summary: Weekly pulse focused on finishing the Quickstart consolidation workstream, stabilizing SDK telemetry v2, pruning stale samples, and shipping a small 'lite' onboarding flow for internal beta customers. We aimed for low-risk deliverables that improve first-run experience and reduce support volume.
notes: Background: After the July rollup we split the onramp work into three parallel streams: SDK telemetry upgrade (v1 -> v2), quickstart consolidation (single canonical repo + language wrappers), and sample pruning/migration to snippets. This week's check concentrates on cleanup work that reduces cognitive load for first-time users.
discussion_points:
1) Quickstarts: finalizing the canonical quickstart repo structure. Proposal accepted: top-level 'getting-started' with language folders (python, node, go, dotnet). Each folder must include a minimal example, env setup, and a smoke-test script.

2) SDK telemetry v2: shipping instrumentation to capture first-run paths, errors during auth, and sample-to-quickstart handoffs. Liam reported telemetry library is feature-complete; integration tests failing for token refresh edge case (related to DI-4521).

3) Samples pruning: Diego proposed archiving 42 stale samples and converting 8 into 'snippets' for the docs snippets registry. Agreed archive branch naming: samples/archive/2026-09.

4) 'Lite' Onramp: Priya demoed a two-step onboarding flow (create API key, run 'hello world' that returns a short streaming response). Goal: reduce time-to-first-success from ~15min to <5min for internal beta.

5) Docs microcopy: Aria presented edits to CLI quickstart copy to reduce confusion around region selection and dedicated vs hosted calls. We will A/B test the new wording in the docs site next week.
decisions:
- Adopt canonical quickstart repo layout as described (getting-started/{language}).
- Archive 42 stale samples; convert 8 to snippets and link from quickstarts.
- Blocker for production rollout of telemetry v2 is token-refresh handling — prioritize DI-4521.
- Ship 'lite' onramp as opt-in beta behind feature flag for a small set of internal accounts.
risks_and_blockers:
- Token refresh edge case in SDK telemetry causing duplicate events (DI-4521) — blocks full rollout of v2.
- Small docs backlog: Snippet indexing to search is slower than expected, could delay links in quickstarts.
- Resource: Diego needs one more backend engineer for the samples migration (ETA if approved: 3 weeks).
